done.why: I got the egg into the trophy case early on, around turn 23. After that I kept going after the rest of the place: the dam, the reservoir, the river and the treasures. I hit the 250-turn limit just as I was putting the platinum bar into the case.

about: It's the white house and the Great Underground Empire again, but some of it has been rewritten. The middle of it is Flood Control Dam #3. You open the sluice gates and the reservoir drains, so you can walk across the mud to a trunk, a trident and an air pump. Then you take a rubber boat down the Frigid River toward Aragain Falls. The house above is the place you keep coming back to, and the chimney only lets you carry up one treasure at a time. A thief hangs around the edges. The egg can only be opened by "deft fingers, and not entirely honest ones," which hints that the thief has some part to play with it.

ending.what: The jewel-encrusted egg went into the trophy case at turn 23 and was still there after I died and came back. By the end the case also held the trunk of jewels, the painting and the crystal trident. The platinum bar was going in on my last turn.

moments.note: The egg was right there in the nest up the tree. The new nest description has a nice line about the songbird's 'better taste in treasure than in architecture'.
The egg went straight into the case. My goal was done with almost no resistance.
Looking at the egg, the clasp 'would take a professional's fingers to undo... not entirely honest ones'. That reads like the thief is supposed to open it.
The troll died in a single blow.
I had queued up several attacks and the troll was already gone, so I wasted six turns on 'You can't see any such thing.' My mistake, but the count still went down.
The dam's green bubble has 'the patient look of something waiting to be told it may begin'. After I pushed the yellow button it was 'glowing serenely'. Nice cause and effect.
Turning the bolt opened the sluice gates. Later the reservoir really was mud I could cross to the trunk.
The stairway up from Atlantis is blocked by a new cave-in. Someone chalked an arrow back the way I came. Clearly a deliberate edge to the map.
In the studio the chimney says 'you, your lamp and one thing more'. It still refused me after I dropped four things, because I was holding a tan label I'd forgotten about.
I queued a route with one wrong step and ended up lost in the maze, dropping my rope and knife in the troll room on the way. Getting back out took a dozen turns.
The thief was leaning against a wall with his bag, 'over his dead body'. He didn't attack.
In the Loud Room, typing 'take bar' just echoed back 'Bar bar ...'. Saying 'echo' changed the acoustics and I could pick it up.
Floating down the river and opening the red buoy to find an emerald.

I tried 'go west' from the river near the falls to reach the west beach. It said I couldn't go that way, and then I went straight over the falls and died. I lost the emerald and scarab I was carrying.

The death text was kind and specific. Plain things were scattered around the house, valuables rolled into dark corners, and 'somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room'. The case kept the egg.
I found the scarab at East of Chasm and the platinum bar in the Studio. The 'dark corners' were real places I could reach.

wished: To get back upstream or across to the west bank from the east shore without dying at the falls. The river gave me no hint which ways were safe.
To give the egg to the thief and see whether his 'deft fingers' would open the clasp. The case already had it, and I ran out of turns.
To walk over the rainbow at Aragain Falls to the sunlit beach.
To get past the chalked-arrow cave-in above Atlantis toward the 'faint glitter, as of a great many mirrors'.
To have more turns. A completionist gets through 250 fast in a place this size.

lines.line: The clasp is jeweller's work, and would take a professional's fingers to undo without harm: deft fingers, and not, one suspects, entirely honest ones.
lines.why: It's a quiet hint about the egg and the thief. It changed how I thought about the egg once it was in the case.

lines.line: It is dark, and has the patient look of something waiting to be told it may begin.
lines.why: It made the dam panel feel alive, and it pointed me at the buttons.

lines.line: somebody has chalked an arrow on the rubble pointing back the way you came. You take the hint.
lines.why: A funny, honest way to tell me there was nothing past that point.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: A clear rule that shaped every trip I made afterward.

lines.line: anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it, and somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: It turned dying into a scavenger hunt instead of a dead end, and it was true. I found the bar and scarab where it said.

lines.line: It also looks as though it would not care for anything sharp.
lines.why: A warning about the boat and the sword, done with personality.

fun.why: Draining the reservoir, the echo trick, the buoy and the river ride were all satisfying. Dying at the falls, and my own mistakes in the maze and with the troll, cost me a lot of turns.

engagement.why: Even after my stated goal was done at turn 23, I kept wanting to see the dam and the river and fill the case. The new descriptions kept rewarding me for looking at things.

difficulty.why: The egg goal was nearly trivial: climb the tree, take it, walk to the case. The wider world had real puzzles, like the dam, the chimney limit and the echo, and one harsh trap at the falls. That felt right for exploring past the goal.

interestingness.why: The changed parts stood out. The egg's clasp hints at the thief. There are cave-ins with sorted rubble and chalked arrows, a chimney rule stated outright, and a death that sends your valuables to findable corners.

prose.why: The new lines are witty and precise and fit the original's voice: the songbird's architecture, the patient bubble, the boat that dislikes sharp things, the tidy someone who returns the lamp.
